svg.title: How agents actually work
svg.desc: Twelve agent-design concepts, each with its business effect: Prompt architecture; State outside the model; Retrieval, not stuffing; Skills and tools; Grounded answers (RAG); Numbers by rules; Workflows first; Guardrails; Human in the loop; Evals before go-live; Identity and context; Voice agents.
svg.text: The concepts behind every agent I design.
Role, scope, rules and output contract as
layered sections, not a wall of text.
The context window is not a database.
Each turn reads a typed state record,
decides one step, validates it and writes it
back, so long chats don't drift.
long cases finish correctly, in minutes
An agent needs thousands of tokens, not
for numbers, semantic search for meaning,
a keyword index for exact ids.
Each skill has one job, typed inputs and a
narrow permission. The agent picks skills; it
Retrieve from the knowledge base or graph
first, answer only from what came back,
Figures come from versioned rules and
queries. The model explains them and
no invented figures in finance reports
Deterministic steps and approvals, with the
model used inside a step only where
Check every output against facts and policy
(amounts, ids, PII) before it ships; block or
wrong amounts, ids or PII never reach
Consequential actions such as refunds and
A golden set of real cases, a pass
threshold as the gate, re-run on every
The agent acts as the user, with that user's
no permission leaks; security signs off
Language, voice and greeting must all
match, and latency is a feature, not an
callers stay on the line; fewer drop-offs
